en: This course section will be about classes
and objects and about keeping your classes
and objects clean and working with objects
in a clean way.
Now therefore, of course, it won't matter to
you if you are never ever working with
classes or objects in your code, but if you
do work with classes and objects in any way,
even if that's not a 100% object-oriented
style,
then you will get important information out
of this course section.
Because we are going to have a closer look
at classes and objects and we're going to
learn that we can differentiate between
real objects, if we wanna call them like
this, and data structures or data containers
and what that difference is and why it
matters.
We'll have a look at a bunch of
object-oriented principles which even help
you if you're not following a 100%
object-oriented style. We're going to have a
look at the SOLID principles there and at
the Law of Demeter.
And we're also going to take another look at
polymorphism and see how classes can also
help us with that.
It is a concept we already had a look at in
the last course,
Now we're going to take another look in this
section.
Now, this course section will still have a
couple of demos and examples, but it will be
a bit more theory than the last sections
because in this section, we'll have a couple
of core principles and guidelines which you
should be aware of when working with
classes.
